Consonantal i

Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

special adjective

also especial, extraordinary, unique

classical

Cic. Off. 1.12: praecipuum quendam amōrem
Caes. BG 5.54.4: praecipuō semper honōre

praecipuus, praecipua, praecipuum

adjective

special, particular, beyond the ordinary

Lewis & Short: “particular, peculiar, especial (opp. communis)”: more than others get, or more than usual. The adverb praecipuē is “especially” (see particular).

Examples

  • ingeneratque in prīmīs praecipuum quendam amōrem in eōs quī prōcreātī sunt

    and above all nature implants a special love for those one has brought into the worldCic. Off. 1.12

  • 1Lewis & Short cites the passage as Caes. BG 5.52; the Perseus text has it at 5.54.4.

    praeter Aeduōs et Rēmōs, quōs praecipuō semper honōre Caesar habuit1

    except the Aedui and the Remi, whom Caesar always held in special honourCaes. BG 5.54.4

Other words

  • singulāris, singulāre — unique, one of a kind

    adjective, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Imp. Pomp. 3: singulāris eximiaque virtūs (Lewis & Short)

  • eximius, eximia, eximium — exceptional, out of the ordinary

    adjective · also used · classical · Cic. Off. 1.67: ea quae eximia plērīsque et praeclāra videntur (Lewis & Short)

    “Taken out” of the mass (eximō, Lewis & Short).

  • proprius, propria, proprium — special to, peculiar to, one’s own

    adjective · also used · classical · Ov. Met. 6.350: nec sōlem proprium nātūra … fēcit; Traupman 162: proprium ingenium, a special talent

    What belongs to one person or thing and not to others.

  • speciālis, speciāle — particular (as against general)

    adjective, third declension · also used · classical · Sen. Ep. 58.9: genera speciālia (Lewis & Short); Quint. 5.10.43 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 130: pretium speciāle, a special offer

    A term of logic and rhetoric, opposed to generālis, and post-Augustan (Lewis & Short); it does not mean “out of the ordinary”. Traupman’s pretium speciāle (see bargain) is a modern use.

See also particular, general, main, bargain.

SourcesLewis & Short: praecipuus · Lewis & Short: singularis · Lewis & Short: eximius · Lewis & Short: proprius · Lewis & Short: specialis

John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 130, 162.
